name: Pacemaker cell (sinoatrial node)
short_description: Small spindle-shaped nodal myocyte of the sinoatrial node that generates its own electrical impulse: its membrane potential never rests but drifts steadily upward until the cell fires — the body's built-in metronome.

textbook.1: fail (gemini-3-pro-image; the cell was drawn as a jagged LIGHTNING-BOLT silhouette with sharp angular kinks instead of a smooth fusiform spindle - anatomically wrong and exactly the forbidden decorative electricity motif - and the cut-away was rendered as a detached floating RECTANGULAR inset panel sitting apart from the cell, i.e. a second cell fragment plus a box/frame; also a glowing spark flare at the upper tip)
textbook.2: pass (gemini-3-pro-image; smooth slender fusiform spindle cell lying diagonally with two short blunt spider-processes, muted desaturated educational palette on neutral dark charcoal, thin clean outlines, correct cut-away opened in the cell's own wall with ONE central pale-lilac nucleus, only a few short terracotta myofibril strands lying at different angles with faint irregular banding, sparse pale-teal SR web, abundant ochre glycogen granules, a handful of dusty-orange mitochondria, teal caveolae pits plus green HCN4 and blue Ca-channel motifs in the sarcolemma, grey-violet connexin-45 plaques where neighbouring nodal-cell tips abut each tapered end, sage collagen fibres of the nodal matrix; no sarcomere banding, no intercalated discs, no branching, no text, no border)

sem.1: pass (gemini-3-pro-image; false-colour surface-only micrograph of a single slender fusiform nodal cell with two short blunt spider-processes, sarcolemma finely stippled with caveolae pits and shallow folds, small flattened contact plaques where neighbouring cell tips abut the tapering ends, the cell half-nestled in a mat of fine wavy teal-grey collagen fibrils, warm amber false-colour on a dark charcoal background, shallow depth of field, no internal organelles as is correct for SEM, no striated banded surface, no intercalated discs, no text or scale bar; minor note: the tapering ends run off the frame edges, which is typical of a real SEM field and leaves the cell body centred and fully readable)

3d.1: pass (gemini-3-pro-image; translucent spindle-shaped nodal myocyte with subsurface scattering and gentle rim light on a clean dark studio background, natural clearly-distinguishable biological tints - warm cream-rose sarcoplasm, pale-lilac nucleus, terracotta myofibrils, pale-teal SR web, amber glycogen specks, dusty-orange mitochondria, teal caveolae dimples, green HCN4 and blue Ca-channel proteins in the sarcolemma, grey-violet connexin-45 plaques at both tapered ends, sage collagen fibres curving past; not near-monochrome and not neon, single specimen, no sarcomere striations, no intercalated discs, no branching, no text, no border)

watercolor.1: pass (gemini-3-pro-image; warm aged paper fills the whole frame corner to corner with a soft darker wash halo painted directly on it - no mat, frame, drop shadow or sheet-on-a-surface - subject large and centred, fine ink linework over translucent washes, correct slender fusiform spindle with short blunt spider-processes, one central pale-lilac nucleus, few short disorganised terracotta myofibrils with only faint irregular banding, sparse teal SR web, ochre glycogen stipple, a handful of mitochondria, membrane channel and caveolae motifs, a grey-violet gap-junction plaque where a neighbouring cell tip touches the upper end, loose sage collagen fibres; no sarcomere ladder, no intercalated discs, no branching, no text)

reference: pass with caveat (Wikimedia Commons "Sinoatrial node high mag.jpg", CC BY-SA 3.0, Nephron; a genuine high-magnification H&E light micrograph of human sinoatrial-node tissue - pale slender wavy nodal myocyte profiles with single dark elongated nuclei, conspicuously lacking the dense cross-striations of working myocardium, embedded in abundant pale-pink collagenous matrix with small vessels and fibroblast nuclei. Caveat recorded honestly: this is a tissue-section view of the node, not an isolated single pacemaker cell, and at H&E resolution the individual spindle/spider cell outline, sparse myofibrils, caveolae and connexin-45 junctions are not resolvable; no freely-licensed micrograph of a single identified isolated SA-node pacemaker cell could be found. No working-myocyte image was substituted. Cleaned and recomposed with edit_image.py - text/scale-bar/border removal, gentle recompose and contrast restoration, no invented structures)
